newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela 6-month TEM yields fall to 16.99 pct.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela 6-month TEM yields fall to 16.99 pct.

text.p: Yields on Venezuelan benchmark six-month TEMs fell 1.96 basis point to 16.99 in Wednesday's auction, according to a calculation by Reuters that uses the Central Bank formula.

The Central Bank said it sold 20.00 billion bolivars of 180-day "monetary stabilization", or TEM, bills with an 18.95 percent coupon for a price of 100.90 pct. At last week's auction, the six-month notes yielded 18.95 percent.

The bank also sold 5.0 billion bolivars of 269-day notes with a 19.39 percent coupon at a price of 100.03 percent, and 5.0 billion bolivars of 358-day notes with a 19.84 percent coupon at an average price of 99.62 percent.
Yields for these notes fell 1.83 basis point to 19.34 percent for the 269-day bills, and 2.09 basis points to 20.30 percent for the 358-day TEMs.
The weekly TEM bill auctions are the Central Bank's principal tool of monetary policy, used to restrict liquidity and establish a benchmark for wider interest rates.
